subject: Error in requesting modification indices for a fitted lavaan.mi model

messages.author: a061c48a0a34b884
messages.subject: Error in requesting modification indices for a fitted lavaan.mi model
parts:
Hello lavaan community,

I am wanting to request modification indices for a lavaan model conducted on multiply imputed datasets. Specifically, it is a threshold invariance model with a significant chi-square change versus the baseline model (suggesting non-invariance, hence why I want to inspect the mod indices).

My code is

mi1 <- modificationIndices.mi(thresh.fit)

Which produces the error and warning

Error in `$<.data.frame `(`*tmp*`, "mi", value = c(1.46131364303112, 0.458487752314134,  :
    replacement has 1560 rows, data has 1559
In addition: warning message:
In (function (..., deparse.level = 1)  :
    number of rows of result is not a multiple of vector length (arg1)

At the moment, I am running the command with test = "D1", but it is taking a long time to execute (as suggested by the documentation).

Has anyone encountered this issue as well?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error in requesting modification indices for a fitted lavaan.mi model
parts:
Not sure why the number of rows in the parameter table differs from the number of score tests calculated for those rows, but modindices.mi() only provides score tests for fixed parameters.  If you want score tests for equality constraints on estimated parameters, you need to use lavTestScore.mi() and explicitly choose which constraints at the bottom of the parTable() you want to consider whether to release=

messages.subject: Re: Error in requesting modification indices for a fitted lavaan.mi model
parts:
Hi Elena,

I used to have this problem as well (R objects and other packages conflicting with semTools). If you go into Tools > General, make sure "Restore .RData into workspace at startup" is not selected, and (optionally) "Save workspace to .RData on exit" is set to Never.

This means you have to manually save and load any objects you want to keep (using the saveRDS and readRDS functions). But it should fix your issues with namespaces.
